comment.narrative: CSW- WGG representation at the 69th session of the CSW comprised a delegation of representatives from the partners. The virtual side-event organised by WGG titled ‘Practicing disability justice in GBV responses: What feminists need to understand and do better?’ was attended by about 70 participants. The panel drove critical dialogue on how the feminist movement can more effectively integrate disability justice into GBV work. In-person participation of partners helped them connect, share strategies, and amplify voices in global feminist dialogues.

WGG is collaborating in a five-year program (2021-2025), in five priority countries: Bangladesh, India, Kenya, Rwanda, and Uganda, through sixteen strategic in-country partners, several of whom are led by and support persons with disability and young women.

WGG has applied to host event at CSW 2024 titled: Disability justice, youth leadership and systemic gender-based violence:Counternarratives from the Global South.Disabled and young women and gender diverse communities experience many facets of structural violence. This includes persistent disparities when accessing public resources and social rights, particularly related to education and health, as well as when accessing the labor market, and public and decision-making spaces. The disproportionate impact of this exclusion and violence on these communities must be addressed as a priority by states and communities. Disability-led and youth-led organizations in the Global South, while operating in these resource-starved contexts, are offering counternarratives grounded in youth leadership and disability justice. During this event we want to rethink priorities, center their leadership to address institutional change and economic justice.Part payment of sub-grant to IWRAW Asia Pacific; - A partners’ consultation (October 2022) in Bangkok has offered WGG partners with a substantive position vis-à-vis carceral laws, as well as related issues that resonate most with our constituencies. The meeting organized by IWRAW AP (with support from WGG partners) was the first space where WGG partners met. Together, we focused on building a common political agenda, utilzing the findings of the research paper, and in-person consultation with partners. Partners identified key priorities for the meeting including sharing strategies around SGBV advocacy, mapping learning priorities, and creating space for more nuanced conversations around SGBV, prevention, access to justice, alternative approaches, and key feminist histories (globally and regionally) around transformative and restorative justice, and revisiting WGG’s pathways of change. A briefing paper on this issue was delivered in 2023; it will guide us in creating our political agenda around anti-carcerality but also inform our programming and wider work in the future.
